questions.q: How does the JVM decide an object can be garbage collected?
o: It is no longer reachable from any GC root
Its reference count has dropped to zero
It is older than a fixed number of seconds
Its `finalize()` method has been called
questions.w: Java uses reachability tracing from roots (thread stacks, static fields, JNI). Cycles are collected fine because they are unreachable.

questions.q: Why is the heap split into young and old generations?
o: Most objects die young, so frequent cheap young collections pay off
The operating system requires two separate memory regions
Strings must be kept apart from numbers in memory
Class definitions need their own generation
questions.w: The weak generational hypothesis: collect the young generation often and cheaply, promote survivors to old, collect old rarely.

o: All application threads pause while the collector works
The JVM exits and restarts itself after a fatal error
A thread dump is written to disk for later analysis
A network call to another service times out
questions.w: Modern collectors (G1, ZGC, Shenandoah) aim to keep pauses short by doing most of the work concurrently.

questions.q: Which collector is the default in modern JDKs (9+) for server workloads?
o: G1
Serial
CMS
Epsilon
questions.w: G1 splits the heap into regions and targets a pause-time goal. ZGC suits very large heaps with sub-millisecond pauses.

questions.q: A service's heap usage keeps climbing and it ends with `OutOfMemoryError`, although it has no obvious bug. Which is the most likely cause?
o: A leak: objects stay reachable, e.g. in a static map or cache
The garbage collector has been switched off by a flag
The application has been given too few request threads
The disk has filled up with old log files and dumps
questions.w: Java leaks are reachable objects that are no longer needed. Take a heap dump and look at the dominator tree.

questions.q: Which tool or flag helps you capture evidence when an `OutOfMemoryError` occurs?
o: `-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError`, then inspect it in Eclipse MAT
`-Xmx0` to stop the heap from growing any further
Calling `System.gc()` repeatedly in a tight loop
Restarting the whole server once every single hour
questions.w: The dump shows which objects dominate memory and what holds references to them.

o: It only suggests a collection and may be ignored
It forces an immediate full collection every time
It frees native memory outside the heap
It resets the heap size to its default
questions.w: Explicit GC calls can cause long pauses. Fix allocation patterns and tune the collector instead.

questions.q: A service has frequent long pauses caused by many large, short-lived allocations. What is a sensible first step?
o: Measure with GC logs, then cut allocation or tune settings
Sprinkle `System.gc()` calls through the code
Raise the number of request threads
Move the logs to a faster disk
questions.w: Turn on GC logging (`-Xlog:gc*`), look at pause time and frequency, then change one thing at a time.
